fullPassage:
Discovering Yourself through Challenges

"To grow into a better version of ourselves, we should not stay as we are." That was the first thing our teacher said to us on the first day of school. She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our relationships. The important part was trying something new for each one. She told us that we should share our experiences with our classmates when we finished the challenges.

Challenge 1: Ticket for One

These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy.

Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about.

At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story. It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.

Challenge 2: Riding the Waves

Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course.

At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.

Challenge 3: A New Look

Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to draw attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited me.

The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about myself.

I learned a lot about myself through this assignment, and I found out that my classmates did, too. One of them tried new foods from different countries, while another joined a creative writing club. Through these experiences, we all realized how important it is to push ourselves to try new things. We gained different perspectives on life and had a lot of fun, too! My classmates and I even talked about setting more challenges for ourselves. There are always more things that we can discover about ourselves, and it's exciting to keep learning and growing. We never know what we're capable of until we try!

questions.passage: She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our (A)[comfort / control] zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an (B)[assignment / assessment] to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our (C)[relationships / responsibilities]. The important part was trying something new for each one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 우리가 안전지대 밖으로 나가 학기를 시작하기를 바라셨다. 우리에게 세 가지 방식으로 도전할 과제를 주셨다. 세 가지 도전은 취미, 운동, 학업, 심지어 우리의 관계까지 포함할 수 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) comfort: 'comfort zone(안전지대)'은 원문의 핵심 표현. control zone은 부자연스러움. ✅ (B) assignment: 선생님이 준 '과제'. assessment(평가)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) relationships: 취미, 운동, 학업과 나란히 나열된 '관계'. responsibilities(책임)는 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: comfort zone: 자신이 편안하게 느끼는 영역. assignment vs assessment: 과제 vs 평가.

questions.passage: Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt (A)[comfortable / competitive] while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to (B)[overcome / overlook] this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an (C)[indoor / outdoor] pool on social media.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어릴 때부터 물을 두려워해서 물놀이를 하며 편하게 느낀 적이 없었다. 이 불편함을 극복하기로 결심했다. 소셜 미디어에서 사촌이 실내 수영장에서 서핑하는 영상을 보았다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) comfortable: 물을 무서워해 '편안한' 느낌이 없었다. competitive(경쟁적인)는 문맥과 무관. ✅ (B) overcome: 불편함을 '극복'하겠다. overlook(간과하다)은 반대 의미. ✅ (C) indoor: 바다가 아닌 '실내' 수영장. outdoor(야외)는 원문과 반대.
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) vs overlook(간과하다): 접두사 over-가 같지만 의미가 완전히 다름.

questions.passage: Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most (A)[nervous / curious]: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to draw (B)[attention / conclusion] to it. Since I was feeling (C)[confident / cautious] after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 세 번째 도전이 가장 초조하게 했다: 머리 모양 바꾸기. 이마가 넓다고 생각해 주의를 끌고 싶지 않았다. 첫 두 도전 후 자신감을 느껴 미용실에 갔다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) nervous: 머리를 바꾸는 것이 가장 '초조'했다. curious(궁금한)는 부정적 감정과 어울리지 않음. ✅ (B) attention: 'draw attention to(~에 주의를 끌다)'는 관용 표현. draw conclusion(결론을 내리다)은 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) confident: 앞선 도전 성공 후 '자신감'을 느낌. cautious(조심스러운)는 행동과 모순(미용실에 갔으므로).
det.tip: draw attention to: ~에 주의를 끌다. draw conclusion: 결론을 내리다. 같은 draw라도 뒤에 오는 명사에 따라 의미가 달라진다.

questions.passage: Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's ①<u>preferences</u>. I saw the experience as a good ②<u>opportunity</u> to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been ③<u>curious</u> about. At first, it felt a bit ④<u>comfortable</u> and lonely to sit in the theater by myself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혼자 영화관에 가는 것은 처음이었다. 영화와 좌석을 직접 고르는 것이 좋았고, 다른 사람의 선호를 걱정할 필요가 없었다. 사극을 골랐다. 처음에는 혼자 앉는 것이 약간 어색하고 외로웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①preferences(선호): 다른 사람의 선호를 걱정할 필요 없었다. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②opportunity(기회): 다른 것을 볼 좋은 기회. 원문 그대로. ✅ ③curious(궁금한): 궁금했던 사극을 골랐다. 원문 그대로. ❌ ④comfortable(편안한): 원문은 awkward(어색한). 혼자 앉는 것이 '처음'이라 편안할 수 없고, lonely와도 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: awkward(어색한) ↔ comfortable(편안한). 처음 하는 일에서 느끼는 감정은 awkward가 자연스럽다.

questions.passage: One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the ①<u>fact</u> that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She ②<u>denied</u> me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to ③<u>stand</u> up on the board. After some help from the instructor, I learned how to balance ④<u>properly</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사촌이 실내 수영장에서 서핑하는 영상을 보았다. 얕은 수영장이라는 사실이 마음에 들었다. 사촌이 어렵지 않다고 장담해줘서 초보 과정에 등록했다. 보드 위에 서는 것이 어려웠지만 제대로 균형 잡는 법을 배웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①fact(사실): 얕은 수영장이라는 '사실'이 좋았다. 원문 그대로. ❌ ②denied(부인했다): 원문은 assured(장담했다). 사촌이 어렵지 않다고 '장담'해서 등록한 것. denied는 '부인하다'로 정반대 의미. ✅ ③stand(서다): 보드 위에 '서는' 것이 어려웠다. 원문 그대로. ✅ ④properly(제대로): '제대로' 균형 잡는 법을 배웠다. 원문 그대로.
det.tip: assured(장담하다/안심시키다) ↔ denied(부인하다/거절하다). 'She assured me that ~'은 '~라고 안심시켜줬다'는 뜻.

questions.passage: Through these experiences, we all realized how important it is to push ourselves to try new things. We gained different ①<u>perspectives</u> on life and had a lot of fun, too! My classmates and I even talked about setting more challenges for ourselves. There are always more things that we can ②<u>discover</u> about ourselves, and it's ③<u>boring</u> to keep learning and growing. We never know what we're ④<u>capable</u> of until we try!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 경험들을 통해 새로운 것을 시도하는 것이 얼마나 중요한지 깨달았다. 삶에 대한 다양한 시각을 얻었다. 자신에 대해 발견할 것이 항상 있고, 계속 배우고 성장하는 것은 신나는 일이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①perspectives(시각): 삶에 대한 다양한 '관점'을 얻었다. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②discover(발견하다): 자신에 대해 '발견'할 수 있는 것이 많다. 원문 그대로. ❌ ③boring(지루한): 원문은 exciting(신나는). 글의 결론이 '도전의 가치'를 강조하므로 boring은 맥락과 완전히 반대. ✅ ④capable(할 수 있는): 시도하기 전엔 무엇을 '할 수 있는지' 모른다. 원문 그대로.
det.tip: exciting(신나는) ↔ boring(지루한). 글의 전체 톤이 긍정적이므로 결론도 긍정적 단어가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 보통 친구나 가족과 영화를 보는데, 혼자 가니 다른 사람의 선호를 걱정할 필요가 없었다.
det.analysis: ✅ preferences(선호): 다른 사람과 함께 갈 때는 그들의 '취향/선호'를 고려해야 하지만, 혼자 가면 걱정할 필요 없다. ❌ performances(공연): 문맥과 무관. ❌ appearances(외모): 영화 선택과 관련 없음. ❌ differences(차이): 걱정의 대상으로 부자연스러움.
det.tip: preference: '선호, 취향'. 'worry about someone's preferences'는 '누군가의 선호를 걱정하다'.

questions.passage: Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this __________. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어릴 때부터 물을 무서워해서 물놀이를 즐기거나 편하게 느낀 적이 없었다. 이 불편함을 극복하기로 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ discomfort(불편함): 물에 대한 두려움 → 물놀이가 불편한 상태를 '극복'하겠다는 맥락. ❌ discovery(발견): overcome과 어울리지 않음. ❌ distance(거리): 문맥과 무관. ❌ disappointment(실망): 두려움이지 실망이 아님.
det.tip: discomfort: dis-(반대) + comfort(편안함) = 불편함. overcome discomfort: 불편함을 극복하다.

questions.passage: At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely __________ in the story. It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음에는 어색했지만 영화가 시작되자 이야기에 완전히 몰두하게 되었다. 영화 자체에 집중하는 것이 매우 만족스러웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ absorbed(몰두한): 'became completely absorbed in'은 '~에 완전히 빠져들다'. 영화에 집중해 만족했다는 맥락과 완벽히 일치. ❌ abandoned(버려진): 의미 부적합. ❌ disturbed(방해받은): 'nothing to distract me'와 모순. ❌ confused(혼란스러운): 만족스러웠다는 결과와 맞지 않음.
det.tip: be absorbed in: ~에 몰두하다/빠져들다. absorb의 수동태가 '집중' 의미로 쓰이는 고급 표현.

questions.passage: She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an <u>assignment</u> to challenge ourselves in three different ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 assignment와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 선생님이 세 가지 방식으로 도전할 과제를 주셨다.
det.analysis: ✅ task(과업): assignment와 동의어. 둘 다 '해야 할 일/과제'라는 의미. ❌ advantage(이점): 의미 무관. ❌ achievement(성취): 과제가 아니라 결과. ❌ agreement(합의): 문맥과 전혀 다른 의미.
det.tip: assignment = task = 과제. 학교에서 선생님이 주는 과제는 assignment, 직장에서는 task를 더 많이 쓴다.

questions.passage: At first, it felt a bit <u>awkward</u> and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 awkward와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 처음에는 혼자 극장에 앉는 것이 약간 어색하고 외로웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ uncomfortable(불편한): awkward와 가장 가까운 의미. 둘 다 '편치 않은/어색한' 느낌. ❌ exhausting(지치는): 피로감이지 어색함이 아님. ❌ unforgettable(잊을 수 없는): 의미 무관. ❌ unnecessary(불필요한): 감정이 아님.
det.tip: awkward: 어색한, 거북한. 처음 하는 일에서 느끼는 불편한 감정을 표현할 때 자주 사용.

questions.passage: I messaged my cousin about it. She <u>assured</u> me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 assured와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 사촌이 어렵지 않다고 장담해주어서 초보 과정에 등록했다.
det.analysis: ✅ guaranteed(보장했다): assured와 가장 가까운 의미. '확실히 ~라고 말해줌'. ❌ informed(알려줬다): 단순 정보 전달, 안심시키는 느낌 없음. ❌ reminded(상기시켰다): 잊었던 것을 다시 알려주는 것. ❌ requested(요청했다): 완전히 다른 의미.
det.tip: assure: 안심시키다, 장담하다. 'She assured me that ~'은 '그녀가 ~라고 확신시켜줬다'.

questions.passage: The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were <u>positive</u>. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 positive와 반대되는 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: 다음 날 학교에서 반 친구들은 놀랐지만 전반적으로 반응이 긍정적이었다.
det.analysis: ✅ negative(부정적인): positive의 정확한 반의어. ❌ passive(수동적인): 반의어가 아닌 다른 카테고리. ❌ relative(상대적인): 의미 무관. ❌ sensitive(민감한): 반의어 관계 아님.
det.tip: positive ↔ negative: 긍정적 ↔ 부정적. '-ive'로 끝나는 형용사가 여러 개 나오면 의미 혼동 주의.

questions.passage: It was so <u>satisfying</u> just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 satisfying과 반대되는 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: 영화 자체에 집중하는 것이 매우 만족스러웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ frustrating(좌절감을 주는): satisfying의 반의어. 만족 ↔ 좌절. ❌ fascinating(매혹적인): 긍정적 의미라 반의어가 아님. ❌ surprising(놀라운): 감정의 방향이 다를 뿐 반대 아님. ❌ exhausting(지치는): 피로감이지 불만족이 아님.
det.tip: satisfying(만족스러운) ↔ frustrating(좌절감을 주는). '-ing' 형용사끼리의 반의어 관계.

questions.passage:
(A) I had always thought my forehead was large, and I didn't want to <u>draw</u> attention to it.

(B) The art teacher told us to <u>draw</u> a picture of our favorite place during summer vacation.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 draw의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 이마에 주의를 끌고 싶지 않았다. (B) 미술 선생님이 그림을 그리라고 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) '끌다(attract)': 'draw attention to'는 '주의를 끌다'라는 관용 표현. ✅ (B) '그리다(sketch)': 'draw a picture'는 '그림을 그리다'. (A)와 (B)에서 draw가 완전히 다른 의미로 사용됨.
det.tip: draw: ① 끌다(draw attention/conclusion) ② 그리다(draw a picture/map) ③ 뽑다(draw a card). 다의어는 앞뒤 문맥으로 의미를 파악해야 한다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a feeling of slight pain or unease that makes it hard to relax or enjoy something"

det.korean: "무언가를 편히 쉬거나 즐기기 어렵게 하는 약간의 고통이나 불안감"
det.analysis: ✅ discomfort(불편함): '편히 쉬기 어렵게 하는 느낌'에 정확히 부합. dis-(반대) + comfort(편안함). ❌ adventure(모험): 불편함이 아닌 흥미로운 경험. ❌ assignment(과제): 해야 할 일이지 감정이 아님. ❌ preference(선호): 좋아하는 것이지 불편함이 아님.
det.tip: 영영풀이에서 핵심 단서: 'hard to relax(쉬기 어려운)' + 'unease(불안감)' → discomfort.

questions.passage: Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. It required a lot of courage to go by myself. However, my __________ (decide) to try it turned out to be a great choice. I really enjoyed the experience of watching a movie alone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 혼자 영화관에 가려면 많은 용기가 필요했다. 하지만 시도하겠다는 나의 결정은 훌륭한 선택이었다.
det.analysis: decide(동사: 결정하다) → decision(명사: 결정). my + __________ 구조에서 소유격 뒤에 명사가 와야 하므로 decide를 명사형 decision으로 변환.
det.tip: decide(v.) → decision(n.) → decisive(adj.) → decisively(adv.). 품사 변환에서 동사→명사는 -sion/-tion 어미가 대표적.

questions.passage: At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, I learned how to balance __________ (proper) and even managed to surf a few waves!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 강습 초반에는 보드 위에 서기도 힘들었다. 강사의 도움으로 제대로 균형 잡는 법을 배웠다.
det.analysis: proper(형용사: 적절한) → properly(부사: 제대로). 'balance properly'에서 동사 balance를 수식하는 부사가 필요하므로 형용사 proper를 부사형 properly로 변환.
det.tip: proper(adj.) → properly(adv.). '-ly'를 붙여 부사로 바꾸는 가장 기본적인 어형 변환.

questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to __________. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혼자 영화관에 가본 적이 없었는데, 첫 번째 도전으로 시도해 보기로 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ give it a try(시도해 보다): 한 번도 해보지 않은 일을 '시도'하는 맥락. 뒤에 영화와 좌석을 직접 골랐다는 긍정적 결과와 연결. ❌ give it up(포기하다): 도전 시작 단계에서 포기는 모순. ❌ put it off(미루다): 실제로 행동했으므로 미룬 것이 아님. ❌ turn it down(거절하다): 자발적 도전이므로 거절과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: give it a try: 시도해 보다. give up: 포기하다. put off: 미루다. turn down: 거절하다. 구동사의 의미 차이에 주의.

questions.passage: Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to __________ to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이마가 넓다고 생각해서 그것에 주의를 끌고 싶지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ draw attention(주의를 끌다): 'draw attention to'는 '~에 시선을 끌다'. 이마가 넓어서 남들이 보지 않길 바란 맥락. ❌ show concern(걱정을 보이다): 타인에 대한 걱정 표현이지, 외모에 시선 끌기와 무관. ❌ take offense(기분 나빠하다): 이마에 '기분 나빠하다'는 부자연스러움. ❌ make reference(언급하다): 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: draw attention to: ~에 주의를 끌다. 'I didn't want to draw attention to it'은 '그것에 주목받고 싶지 않았다'는 뜻.
